t: You're looking at a statue of Sir Hans Sloane, sculpted by John Michael Rysbrack. Rysbrack was a Flemish sculptor who spent most of his career in England, where he was one of the foremost makers of monuments and portraits in the first half of the eighteenth century. His style mixed Flemish Baroque with classical influences. Sloane was an Anglo-Irish physician, naturalist and collector. He bequeathed his collection of 71,000 items to the nation, which provided the foundation of the British Museum, the British Library and the Natural History Museum.
